newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: LITHUANIAN SHARES UP, DEALERS SAY MORE GAINS POSSIBLE.
newsitem.headline: LITHUANIAN SHARES UP, DEALERS SAY MORE GAINS POSSIBLE.

text.p: Lithuanian shares advanced by the close on Tuesday, as official list banking shares maintained their dominance.
Dealers said there was some optimism that the rise in the market, coming after a prolonged slump, may continue.
Official list shares advanced 11.83 points to 943.92 points, and the broader group A edged up 3.04 points to 1857.61 points.
"A slight trend for an increase should remain until the end of the week, with mainly official list shares going up," said one broker.
The central market traded 853,000 litas versus 539,000 litas, while turnover in block trades was 3.1 million litas versus 3.4 million litas.
Official list favourites Hermis Bank and Vilniaus Bank remained dominant in central market trade. Hermis shares held firm at 210 litas and turned over 339,000 litas.
Hermis saw 1.7 million litas turnover in block trades at 170.10 litas.
Vilniaus Bank advanced to 243.20 litas from 240 litas on the central market amid 138,000 litas turnover.
Vilniaus Bank said on Monday its profit for the first six months was 21.4 million litas.
Hermis said last week its first-half profit was 14.3 million litas but dealers say Hermis shares still have more room to grow than Vilniaus Bank's.
"It's cheap compared to Vilniaus Bank and the results were good," said one dealer.
Group A standout was the Lithuanian Sea Shipping Company as it sunk to 5.29 litas from 5.87 litas in fairly quiet central market turnover of about 11,000 litas.
"I think the price should return to its normal level, 5.80 litas to 5.90 litas, or at least to 5.70 litas tomorrow," one broker said. "I think technical reasons brought the price down."
TV screen producer Ekranas slid to 4.90 litas from 5.35 litas on the central market in low trade of about 7,000 litas.

Ekranas said on Monday its profit for the first six months was 8.6 million litas in the first six months of 1997 but has complained that an unfavourable exchange rate between the dollar and German mark was hurting its sales.
"This (the fall in share price) was caused by the comany's announcement that the dollar-mark rate was hurting them," one dealer said.
